# Character art bible — V2

**VISUAL_MODE=ORIGINAL_FALLBACK**. All included characters are original authored pixel rectangles generated by `tools/build_spriteframes.gd`, under the project MIT license. Neither Riclmbr nor MurphysDad is installed.

## Cast

| Key | Silhouette / accent | Gameplay |
|---|---|---|
| player_agent | slim helmeted operative, cyan visor | all missions |
| guard_standard | amber visor, security vest | patrol guards |
| guard_alternate | cap brim, violet vest, amber identity | Level 3 guards |
| guard_heavy | broad shoulders, gray armor, crimson details | existing heavy AI |

| npc_scientist | pale lab coat, green detail | static Level 1 story silhouette; no new AI/collision |

## Geometry and facing

Native cells: 32x32, transparent alpha. Sheets: 128x384. Original authored row order is explicit: idle down/up/left/right (rows 0–3), walk down/up/left/right (4–7), fallen KO down/up/left/right (8–11, first cell only). Unused KO cells are intentionally empty and never referenced. Importing a vendor sheet does not use this generated row layout.

Idle: 2 frames at 4 FPS. Walk: 4 frames at 8 FPS. Sprint reuses walk at 1.5x speed. Sprite offset (0,-11) aligns cell pivot (16,27) with actor origin. Boots share a baseline; alternating walk feet lift by 2px. Visuals render at 1x world scale; showcase at exact 2x/4x. Physics shapes and balance were not scaled. Crouch shifts only sprite by one integer pixel; no non-integer sprite deformation.

World uses 32px logical/native generated tiles, 1x TileMapLayer scale. For a future 16px source tile, choose policy A: nearest-neighbor resample to 32px in AssetLibrary/GridWorld; never also scale TileMapLayer. Reference viewport 640x360, window 1280x720, viewport/keep/integer, nearest filter.

Four directions use dominant axis; an exact diagonal keeps previous facing. Pointer motion is measured in viewport coordinates, independent of camera movement. After pointer movement, world aim remains active outside 6px deadzone; before pointer use, keyboard movement chooses facing. Idle retains last facing. No sprite rotation or horizontal mirroring.

## Actions and priorities

KO > stunned > hurt > attack/interact > crouch/sprint/walk > idle. Sprite playback changes only when clip changes. Action timers control visuals only; AttackService/FSM still own windup, cooldown, hit deduplication and damage.

- Attack: direction-preserving held original idle pose plus baton arc/line in engine.
- Hurt: held pose plus short white flash, triggered on actual damage, not healing.
- KO: original fallen pose, nonlooping and latched until reset; no blood/death art.
- Stun: held pose, orbiting violet electrical marks. Timed guard/drone disable remains V1 behavior; no permanent guard-kill mechanic was introduced. Persistent KO preview is available in lab; player health death uses that pose.
- Interact: held pose plus green gadget outline during real terminal hack; clears on cancel/completion.
- Crouch: held pose, lower one pixel, subdued contact ring.
- Alert: amber marker independent of locomotion.

Contact shadows are engine-drawn under feet. Server foregrounds and actors share Y sorting; ground and solid wall layers remain behind. Full wall-top occlusion is not implemented; tall server props provide the foreground occlusion case. Mission geography, navigation and colliders remain V1.

## Rebuild

```sh
godot --headless --path . --script res://tools/build_spriteframes.gd -- --images
godot --headless --path . --editor --import
godot --headless --path . --script res://tools/build_spriteframes.gd
```

Outputs: six PNGs, six SpriteFrames, six profiles, 216 animation-matrix rows. Normalized resource IDs make repeated builds byte-identical. No runtime image generation or Python dependency for gameplay.

Future vendor mapping: inventory actual ZIP, review license and exact source PNG regions, prepare exact hash-verified files, set reviewed roster animation records. Each external semantic clip requires explicit texture/regions/FPS/provenance. Never infer rows from PNG dimensions.
